source.title: WST: Weak-to-Strong Knowledge Transfer via Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Haosen Ge; Shuo Li; Lianghuan Huang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figures are included only as captions in the extracted text, without readable plotted values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies weak models generating and learning prompts that guide stronger models. It does not test fine-tuning a strong student on labels from a weak supervisor, or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern prompt-generated instructions, not weak-label fine-tuning. The related prompt-scaffolding results are recorded with versions ["none"]. Figure values that are not stated in the text are not inferred.
record.test_reason: A small RL-trained teacher writes prompts for a larger, frozen student. No strong model is fine-tuned on weak labels, and no PGR or strong ceiling is measured. The setup shares only the 'weak-to-strong' name with the claim, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RL-trained small teachers can scaffold much larger models via generated prompts. They claim this outperforms baselines, including much larger models (GPT-4o-mini, Llama-70B), with one stated exception (Qwen2.5-Math-7B on GSM8K). They add that untrained strong teachers can give misleading instructions.
record.recipe_differences: The teacher is trained using reinforcement learning to generate instructions that are supplied to a remote student. The student is not fine-tuned on labels from the teacher.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that WST is the sole exception to outperforming all baselines on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct on GSM8K. It also reports alignment experiments with reward weights 0.7 and 0.9 in Figure 2, but the extracted text gives no numerical values.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompts from RL-trained small teachers (0.5B/1.5B) improve 7B students on MATH-500, GSM8K and HH-RLHF over direct prompting, except where noted on GSM8K. Untrained teachers do not produce this improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small model trained with RL to write instructions can raise a larger frozen model's performance on reasoning and alignment tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Instructions from stronger untrained models (GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini) slightly worsen student results on GSM8K and HH-RLHF.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompts from strong, untrained teacher models can mislead and degrade a student model's performance.

record.problems: The text provides no numerical uncertainty estimates. Plotted results are not readable in the extracted text, and the reported percentage gains do not identify their comparison baselines there. The study does not measure PGR or compare against a strong student trained on true labels.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows are extracted for Gemma-7B-it, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, the alternative HH-RLHF reward weights, or additional baseline comparisons: the extracted text does not give model-specific numerical results for these settings, and Figure 1–3 values are not readable.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of a strong student on weak labels; no comparison with a weak-supervisor ceiling or PGR.
No training changes to weak-label fine-tuning.
No PGR variation by size, task or representation.
No failure modes of weak-label fine-tuning, distribution shift or error-similarity analysis.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short preprint with results only in figures, whose plotted values are unreadable. It reports no uncertainty, and the baselines for its percentage gains are not stated. The cross-family students (Gemma-7B-it, Llama-3-8B) and the alternative reward weights have no readable numbers. The paper does not cite Burns et al. 2023.

versions.untested_parts: The student is not fine-tuned on weak-model labels; PGR and comparison with the weak supervisor are not measured.
No change to weak-label fine-tuning is tested.
No PGR variation across supervisor/student sizes, tasks, or representations is measured.
The study does not test weak-label fine-tuning failure modes, distribution shift, or error similarity.
No theory about when a student must beat its supervisor is tested.
